PE and Sport Premium
As a school and nursery we are great believers in the importance of high- quality PE and sports provision for all of our children. A quality PE and sports curriculum will:
All of our teachers teach a full PE curriculum to ensure good coverage of a wide range of sports and activities. We also work with a fully qualified sports coach who delivers fantastic lessons to each class on a weekly basis.
On occasions through the academic year we have a range of other sporting groups and teams such as climbing wall, scooter and skateboarding that come in which hugely enriches the opportunities we can offer and further excites and motivates the children.
As part of the Heath Academy Trust each year group will have at least one competitive event that they participate in. From dance competitions to tag rugby children love making friendships across schools and of course competing for the all important cup and medals!
Please read the information below which gives details of our PE and Sport Premium Grant and how we allocate the funding.

Our Creative Curriculum
Our Creative Curriculum
We strive to make our curriculum as exciting and engaging for our children as possible. It is created around the children's needs and interests as well as teaching them a wide range of objectives which gives them the skills and knowledge needed to be successful in life.
At St. James' we believe that learning best happens when it is built upon previous knowledge and where it is linked within a range of related subjects. For example: a maths skill may be used in PE and Science , historical learning may support English writing topics etc.... Through this approach, we know that children achieve more, they understand and remember and they are far more excited about their learning.
To find our more about our Curriculum please have a look through the tabs below and look at some of the exciting topics we have been working on so far.... If you would like to know more, contact the school and we'll happily talk you through and show you round!

Maths - How we teach Maths in our School
At St. James' CE First School and Nursery we use Inspire Maths to all of our children from the end of year R- 4.
This is scheme that moves through 3 stages of learning – Concrete, Pictorial and Abstract and enables the children to learn mathematical concepts thoroughly so they develop a better understanding on maths as a whole.
In reception we use a variety of Numicon and concrete resources to help children process mathematical skills and we also include opportunities for Maths investigation through our play activities.
To find out more visit the Inspire Maths website.

SEN
Through our Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) offer At St James' CE First School and Nursery we believe that all children deserve to reach their full potential. We will always strive to provide the best support for any child with Special Education Needs or a disability.
Our Inclusion Coordinator is Mrs Kathryn Cousins. Our Local School Committee Member with responsibility for SEND is Lynne Nash. We have well trained staff who work hard to support pupils with SEND and ensure that they continue to achieve good progress during their time at our school. Every pupil will have the opportunity to learn all of the National Curriculum subjects at the level that suits their ability. We are committed to narrowing the attainment gap between pupils with SEND and those who do not. This may include school interventions, home-school learning programmes or other learning interventions developed on an individual needs basis.
If your child has SEND and you would like to know more about what support we can offer at St James' CE First School you can contact us on:
T: 01425 653063 E: office@alderholt.dorset.sch.uk
Complaints about SEND provision:
If you want to complain about a school’s SEN support, you should do it while your child is still registered at the school.
This includes complaints that the school has not provided the support required by your child’s SEN statement or education, health and care (EHC) plan.
Follow these steps in order. Move on to the next step if your complaint is not resolved.
Complain to the Education Funding Agency instead of the local authority if both the following apply:
Follow the school’s complaints procedure.
Complain to your local authority.

Attendance Procedures
We are committed to ensuring that all children have access to high quality education however we do appreciate there are times when children fall ill or need to have time away from school.
If your child is poorly then please either call the school office to notify us, each day of the absence, and leave a message on our automated phone system or leave a message via parentmail.
If you are running late for drop-off, a quick call to the office will alert us that you are on your way and will prevent your child being marked absent in the register. When you arrive you will be asked to sign your child in via our
E-Reception facility.
If you would like to request absence during term time then you will need to put this request into writing, addressed to the headteacher. Each individual case will be considered on its own merits.
The headteacher carries out attendance monitoring each half term and we are committed to working alongside you where we have a cause to improve attendance.

English - How we teach English in our School
At St. James' CE First School & Nursery we use a phonic and reading programme called Read Write Inc to teach the children their phonic sounds. It also teaches them how to apply those sounds throughout all that they read and write.
The programme also enables the children to build up their comprehension and understanding of what they read through writing activities linked to the books they read.
In addition to the reading they do in Read Write Inc, we also hear children read regularly through Guided reading sessions and individually in class.
For more information on Read Write Inc visit the Read Write Inc Website
Once off the RWI programme children have daily English lessons incorporating reading, writing and SPAG. We like to ensure that we make cross curricular links for writing wherever and whenever possible and we write though all curriculum areas.

Optional Light tea £1.00, variety of options available
Cost of healthy fruit based snacks and milk is included in the fees.
Help with Fees and Funding
St. James' CE First School and Nursery also accepts employers pay scheme childcare vouchers. The following government website has information about tax free childcare, vouchers and funding that maybe suitable for your family; Homepage | Best Start in Life
Tax Free Childcare from HMRC provides 20% towards fee costs.
The government provides FREE 15 hours of Nursery Funding for all 3 and 4 year olds and 2 year olds who meet certain criteria.
For eligible working families in England with children aged 9 months to 4 years there is 30 hours funding available
We always aim to be as flexible as possible and work with you to tailor sessions around you and your child's needs. Further terms and conditions are available from the school office.

Forest Nursery
Here at St James’ we offer Forest School Nursery provision that provides an encouraging, inspiring environment where children can play and learn using all their senses to explore and investigate the world around them.
Our Forest School follows the ethos of developing children's personal, social, academic and emotional development through daily outdoor time in our mature woodland grounds.
Here, the children are given time and space to explore and play, develop skills, interests and understanding through a range of exciting and self-directed experiences.
Introducing a range of stimulus, children use tools, learn boundaries of behaviour and learn to assess risk. Children are given encouragement to direct their own learning helping them grow in confidence and self-esteem and become self-motivated. Our experienced staff are always on hand to observe the children’s learning which is then developed further and scaffolded to incorporate new concepts and ideas.
"Along with milk and vegetables, kids need a steady diet of rocks and worms
Rocks need skipping.
Water needs splashing.
Bugs and frogs and slimy stuff need finding!" - Anon

Forest School
Throughout every child’s school journey we continue to use our mature onsite woodland to enhance, support and facilitate children’s learning.
As practitioners we know that it is the process that learners go through, rather than the outcomes, that can have a profound and lasting impact on them and taking the learning into their natural environment can do just that.
Be it maths, science, geography, art and design (to name just a few) we like to take as much of our learning outdoors as possible. The objectives covered on the curriculum can be secured whilst at the same time providing opportunities for each individual to develop, grow, explore and take chances in a safe but challenging environment.
Children are taught various tool skills from an early age which culminate in fire lighting. It is these behaviours and attitudes that are developed through the Forest School ethos and learning process that develop the reflective and independent, confident and creative, happy and emotionally-aware learners that we want our children to be.
"The best Classroom and the richest classroom is roofed only by the sky!"
